item.content:encoded:

item.title: A first for CRISPR: powerful prime editing alters DNA directly in the human body
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03371-x

Application of the high-precision technique is part of a clinical trial to treat a genetic disease that can cause liver and nerve damage.

item.title: Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03389-1

item.title: Daily Briefing: Tiny doses of LSD seem to boost cognition
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03374-8

The drug improved the ability to focus — but only in women. Plus, US climate scientists are facing a deluge of public-records requests and why a sleep-disorder drug might be the next big blockbuster.
item.dc:title: Daily Briefing: Tiny doses of LSD seem to boost cognition
item.dc:creator: Flora Graham

item.title: Daily briefing: How to rebuild science from ruin
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03363-x

Researchers in New Orleans share lessons from the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina. Plus, budding cryptographers are using AI to crack historical codes and an enzyme that keeps cognition sharp with age.
item.dc:title: Daily briefing: How to rebuild science from ruin
